significance.justification: A verified-true result would license the form-(iii) conclusion that the probe-defined truth belief increases with independently measured entity familiarity, peaks in the "recognized-but-unknown cell," and predicts later associated hallucination, together with the form-(ii) mechanism that an identifiable component causally carries this leak and can be steered. This establishes both a graded behavioral phenomenon and a mechanism, constraining which knowledge conditions should produce false belief and hallucination rather than merely showing that truth or recognition is decodable; this connection is consequential because Geometry of Truth and Do I Know This Entity? treat truth and entity recognition as useful internal signals whose interpretation would need qualification if they systematically interact. The primary H2 statement is determinate, and a negative result would rule out recognition-to-truth contamination as an explanation of familiarity-driven errors, although failures of the bundled localization or linearity subclaims would be less decisive. Topic substitution fails: generic research on LLM beliefs would not itself earn this score because the specific graded ordering, predictive coupling, and causal transport claim are doing the substantive work.

reach.justification: The named handle is the "per-claim recognition-to-truth leak," proposed as a predictor supporting "retrieval gating when recognition is high but knowledge is low, and abstention calibrated on leak magnitude." It is ex ante because the claim says the leak is "read before any query" and predicts hallucination, leaving an action window for systems that audit, gate, or deploy models rather than serving only as a post-hoc explanation. After per-model re-extraction, the claimed graded relation—largest for recognized-but-unknown items and coupled to hallucination—still predicts a qualitative ordering, although the submission explicitly leaves transfer to "very large closed models" uncertain and supplies no architecture-independent numerical law. Topic substitution again fails: the topic alone provides neither this leak score nor its retrieval/abstention rule, so the reach comes from a specific transferable diagnostic with practitioner uptake.
